decisions.rationale: No comparator is the same MCP host-capability projection boundary. Container resource persistence and external projection reconciliation are near-neighbors, but they have distinct state ownership and cleanup or consumer lifecycles.

The anchor owns MCP identity join-back and requested/effective availability transitions. OpenCode blocked UI, generic MCP health recovery, and projection reconciliation consume similar state but have different consumers and transition authority.

No comparator combines MCP credential revocation with read-only APM and trust disclosure lifecycle. The credential concept control, plugin observability, and MCP health recovery are separate authority or consumer contracts.
The MCP password control is a credential-lifecycle near-neighbor, but it does not own OAuth account, tenant, audience, client sharing identity or recursive schema exposure.

MCP portable-entry representation and canonical availability reconciliation are not duplicated. Health recovery, projection drift, and command materialization touch downstream states or execution trust under distinct lifecycles.

No comparator owns the same MCP managed-session pool, refresh, eviction, and teardown lifecycle. Server health, recovery controls, OpenCode retry, and generic MCP health are plausible neighbors with distinct runtime owners or narrower transitions.

Retired Gemini CLI MCP setup lineage is uniquely bounded. Concept-lineage governance, OpenCode lineage, compatibility aliases, and active coding-agent projections have different authority, chronology, or migration lifecycles.
The four-flow MCP owner taxonomy is not repeated. MCP concept controls, credential handling, and health recovery are subordinate or consumer operations with separate lifecycle authority.

No comparator is the same MCP GUI row, inspector, action, and aggregate-status contract. The listed settings, blocked-state, plugin GUI, recovery, and provider disclosure features are distinct surfaces or consumers.

First-run MCP readiness and privacy-safe profile overlays are not duplicated. Credential, provider-account, external projection, consumer-matrix, and migration records have separate disclosure or projection lifecycles.

MI-001 migration-bridge retirement is a specific MCP lineage boundary. Other lineage, alias, owner-map, and projection-migration features have different artifacts, consumers, and retirement authority.

Third-party MCP config review and activation is not the same feature as archive import, overlay ingestion, outbound projection reconciliation, target-file writing, or command materialization, though their trust and transaction boundaries are adjacent.
No comparator owns deterministic MCP schema-record retention. Web result-cache retention is a data-lifecycle neighbor with a different record type, owner, consumer, and invalidation contract.

The overlapping MCP lazy-catalog and descriptor-cache authority is unique. Model or skill discovery, web cache, and external projection drift are plausible cache/discovery neighbors but differ in records, consumers, or refresh lifecycles.

Typed MCP parameter fidelity plus runtime header-secret lifecycle is not repeated. MCP password handling and vision privacy are related security concerns with different data, consumers, and execution boundaries.

The anchor's MCP runtime-call timeout, heartbeat, interrupt, grace, and receipt contract is not duplicated. Health labels, recovery actions, retry races, and promoted MCP health policy cover adjacent but distinct state machines or consumers.

MCP lazy tool exposure and schema-context budgeting is not the same feature as model discovery, skill scan limits, automation availability reporting, or project retrieval budgets; each has distinct inputs and consumers.

Media SSOT ownership and DRY routing are not duplicated as a media feature. Plugin ownership, migration owner maps, tool-summary deferral, and the generic DRY anchor are governance neighbors with different owned product records.

Per-route media input, output, and generated-media truth is not repeated. OpenCode capability use, web operation matrices, provider expansion, support tiers, and coding-agent projection matrices serve different operation families or consumers.

The deficient media capabilities.get entry shape is not duplicated. OpenCode usage alignment, automation availability records, and web dispatcher output schemas are wire-contract neighbors for different authorities and consumers.

OpenAI image route-family separation and its runtime-green gate are not duplicated. External provider lineage, model-native auth, and coding-agent projection matrices use different providers, route types, and evidence lifecycles.

The common media request envelope and provider-extension problem has no same-feature comparator. Web dispatcher results and BrowserAction inputs are schema neighbors owned by distinct operation families.

Direct-provider media evidence scoping is not duplicated. OpenCode lineage, vision bridge boundaries, provider capability expansion, and coding-agent projection examples have distinct evidence subjects or consumers.

The contradictory media disabled-reason vocabulary is unique. Blocked UI, capability availability, blocked-versus-failed taxonomy, support tiers, and provider error mapping use distinct state families and consumers.

Antigravity public catalog and private internal image routes are not duplicated. Provider lineage, model-native auth, coding-agent consumers, and projection migration address different providers or configuration lifecycles.

Antigravity media-catalog refresh, snapshot, and offline behavior is not repeated. Model discovery, web fallback, provider enablement, change tracking, and external projection drift have different data sources and recovery owners.

The setup_hint required-versus-optional contradiction is specific to the media capability response. Automation availability is a related typed-disclosure contract with a separate schema and consumer set.

Media route and account selection has no duplicate. Web provider routing and model-native account identity are near-neighbors, but different operation families own their eligibility, fallback, and user promise.

The concurrent media identity envelope is not duplicated. OpenCode correlation, tool-call correlation, terminal identity, and long-running persistence use distinct runtimes, records, or storage consumers.

The media request lifecycle lacks its own idempotency, cancellation, deadline, and attempt linkage. Transport, retry, batch web, research, web-job, and persistence contracts are near-neighbors under distinct operation authorities.

Media artifact-before-manifest crash consistency is not repeated. Archive commits, browser screenshot artifacts, web cache writes, and long-running persistence have different artifact owners and recovery state machines.

The media failure enum and provider-detail representation are unique. OpenCode normalization, stream arbitration, blocked taxonomy, web-provider error mapping, and platform output parsing have distinct errors and consumers.

Failure and partial-output media usage accounting is not duplicated. Capability usage, provider stream continuity, web jobs, and operation persistence concern different accounting or terminal-state consumers.

Generated prompt and media-artifact privacy is not duplicated. Vision, browser capture, workflow logs, web cache, browser profiles, and operation payloads have separate sensitive data, access, and retention lifecycles.

Media generation supersession has no same-feature comparator. Stream terminal arbitration, web-job concurrency, and persistent operation outcomes are state-record neighbors with distinct schemas and owners.

The media-controls delimiter regex bug is specific to its prompt grammar. Extract normalization and platform output parsers are parsing neighbors with different input languages, authority, and failure behavior.
Multi-kind media prompt classification is not duplicated. Generic normalization precedence and platform output representation precedence operate on different inputs and lifecycle stages.

Media model-token extraction and alias resolution is not repeated. Plugin aliases, skill identity collisions, discovery order, typed precedence, and output parsing have distinct namespaces and consumers.

Media numeric control validation and route-aware billing bounds are unique. LSP timings, discovery resources, retrieval budgets, and web traversal scales have different units, owners, and failure contracts.

Negative-prompt extraction and final prompt cleanup are not duplicated. Platform output parsing is a plausible text-rewrite neighbor but has a different direction, authority, schema, and failure promise.
The stale Gemini-default backend copy is a media-specific user promise. OpenCode lineage or discovery and provider disclosure accessibility are related but do not own this route-support message.

The media capability picker's accessible disabled-state refresh is not duplicated. Plugin GUI, pre-offer browser disclosure, and provider status accessibility are separate surfaces with different actions and state sources.
After exhaustive comparison, no comparator plausibly owns enabled media-capability prompt insertion or its composer merge, caret, undo, and replacement-confirmation lifecycle.
Canonical media strings and their missing localization contract are not duplicated. Plugin GUI and provider status localization are distinct surfaces and message catalogs.
Media tool omission-versus-disabled policy is not repeated. OpenCode blocked or usage states, MCP health recovery, and automation availability are separate capability families and consumers.

The compatibility-only Gemini setup phrase is not duplicated. Plugin aliases, GitHub command migration, a misleading Playwright token, and projection migration have distinct token owners and sunset lifecycles.

Accepted media units retaining unresolved split recommendations are not duplicated. Unoperationalized catalog lifecycle alternatives and unowned risk closure are nearby readiness issues with different units and adjudication authority.

Authorization and redaction for the complete capability registry answer is not duplicated. Credential secrecy, browser disclosure, automation availability, provider expansion, and status accessibility have narrower or different consumers.

Media capability snapshot revisioning and stale-result suppression are not duplicated. Model discovery, MCP health, web routing, provider enablement, change tracking, and projection reconciliation own distinct snapshots or state transitions.

Support telemetry for media capability evaluation and refresh is not duplicated. Diagnostic vocabularies, OpenCode event normalization, plugin observability, and tool correlation are separate emitters and record consumers.

The missing queued-through-recovery state machine for long-running media is not duplicated. OpenCode transport, batch web, research, Docker, web-job, and persistence lifecycles have different operation authorities and terminal promises.

Cursor generated-media output proof is not duplicated. OpenCode lineage, vision bridge routes, provider-only expansion, and coding-agent projection models have different evidence subjects and capability consumers.
